sites.name: Elizabeth Lake Nature Preserve Varga Archaeological Site
sites.description: The preserve includes a complex of archaeological sites associated with Native American occupation in northeastern Illinois.

sites.name: Powers-Walker House at Glacial Park
sites.description: Archaeological investigations at the 1854 Greek Revival farmhouse are presented through exhibits and public programs at the site.

sites.name: Elgin Area Historical Society & Museum
sites.description: Museum exhibits include the E. Maude and Carl Parlasca Native American Collection, housed in Old Main, an 1856 building that was once part of the Elgin Academy.

sites.name: St. Charles History Museum
sites.description: The museum has over 25 exhibits on local history, including American Indian stone artifacts and handicrafts.

sites.name: Pullman National Historical Park
sites.description: Historic archaeology exhibits include artifacts recovered from the site and buildings identified through archaeological excavations.

sites.name: Schingoethe Center for Native American Cultures
sites.description: Exhibits include collections of Native American cultural materials displayed at Aurora University.
sites.notes: Recently relocated/reopened; confirm current public schedule.

sites.name: Addison Historical Museum
sites.description: Located in the 1892 Balzer House, this local historical museum includes an exhibit with area American Indian artifacts.

sites.name: Winfield Mounds Forest Preserve
sites.address: Winfield Rd between Geneva Rd and High Lake Rd
sites.description: The three conical mounds within the forest preserve are thought to date to the Late Woodland period, between AD 600 and 1000.

sites.name: Warrenville Historical Museum
sites.description: Permanent exhibits include a display of Native American artifacts collected by an area family.

sites.name: Mitchell Museum of the American Indian (Gichigamiin Indigenous Nations Museum)
sites.hours: Mon-Fri 10AM-5PM; Sat 10AM-3PM; Sun closed; closed on major holidays
sites.description: Exhibits focus on North American Indian art, culture, and history, including some prehistoric archaeological materials.

sites.name: Potawatomi Village Marker
sites.address: Forest Home Cemetery, 863 S. Des Plaines Ave.
sites.description: The Forest Home Cemetery, once the location of a Potawatomi village and burial ground, has a historical monument noting its location.
sites.notes: Marker location within Forest Home Cemetery.

sites.name: Chicago Portage National Historic Site
sites.description: In 1673 Marquette and Jolliet became the first Europeans known to traverse the portage between the Great Lakes and the Mississippi River system.
sites.notes: Outdoor site in forest preserve land.

sites.name: Field Museum
sites.description: Exhibits include materials from Illinois archaeological sites within broader natural history and ethnographic displays.

sites.name: Plainfield Historical Society Museum
sites.hours: Tue-Thu 9AM-12PM; Sat 1-4PM; other times by appointment
sites.description: Located in an old grain elevator office on Illinois Route 126, the museum has a display of local Native American artifacts.

sites.name: Isle a la Cache Museum
sites.description: Located on a 107-acre island in the Des Plaines River, museum exhibits recreate the fur trade era of the 18th century, when French traders encountered the native Potawatomi. The site features a replica Native American longhouse.

sites.name: Joliet Iron Works Historic Site
sites.address: Columbia Street, just east of Rte. 53 (Scott St.) and east of the Ruby St. Bridge
sites.description: Archaeological investigations at this important industrial site showed that the foundations of 19th-century blast furnaces and related facilities are still present and can be viewed along a 0.59-mile interpretive walking trail.

sites.name: Oakwood Mound
sites.description: This low, broad burial mound is located in Oakwood Cemetery, Joliet, opposite the intersection of Walnut Street and U.S. 30; the 1,000-year-old Woodland period Indian burial mound may be a little older than the Briscoe Mounds. Excavations conducted by the University of Chicago in 1928 yielded, in addition to weapons, ornaments, and implements, the scattered skeletal remains of over 300 persons.

sites.name: Higginbotham Woods Earthwork
sites.address: Joliet, IL; from U.S. 30 west of the I-80 interchange, go north on Gougar Rd.
sites.description: The remaining mound, now in a City of Joliet park, was part of a Potawatomi village and burial ground located on the south side of Hickory Creek.
sites.notes: Half of a mound can be seen about 175 yards north of the Rock Island Railroad tracks and 20 yards west of Gougar Road.

sites.name: Briscoe Mounds
sites.description: Situated along the northern side of the Des Plaines River valley, this mound and village site is affiliated with the Langford tradition of the Upper Mississippian, dating to around AD 1200-1500. The mounds are the largest Native American burial mounds in northern Illinois.
sites.notes: Directions in revision memo: I-55 Bluff Road Exit, then south via the frontage road towards Channahon, IL.

sites.name: Putnam County Historical Society Museum
sites.hours: Pulsifer House: Wed & Fri 10AM-3PM; Agriculture and Historical Museum: 1st Saturday each month 9AM-1PM
sites.description: Exhibits include locally collected Native American artifacts within displays on county and agricultural history.

sites.name: LaSalle County Historical Society Museum
sites.description: The LaSalle County Historical Society has six facilities in total, but three in one place: the Canal Warehouse Museum, the Heritage Center, and the Aitken One-Room School House. The Warehouse Museum is housed in a former limestone warehouse erected in 1848 for the Illinois & Michigan Canal. It includes extensive displays of Native American artifacts, including those excavated from the Grand Village of the Kaskaskia, located across the Illinois River from Starved Rock. Other exhibits on the campus focus on the 19th century, coal mining in Illinois, the early 20th century, and the Civil War.

sites.name: Starved Rock State Park
sites.hours: Trails: Daily 7AM-Sunset; Visitors’ Center: Daily 9AM-4PM except federal holidays Nov-Mar and Juneteenth
sites.description: Starved Rock State Park stretches for miles along the south bank of the Illinois River, beginning at Route 178 and extending east to Illinois Canyon. Archaeological research demonstrated the region has been continuously occupied since it was settled by Native Americans early in the Paleoindian period. Exhibits at the Visitors’ Center have displays on every period, from prehistory to the present.

sites.name: Grundy County Historical Society
sites.description: Exhibits document county prehistory and history, including locally collected artifacts.

sites.name: Illinois and Michigan Canal National Heritage Area (Canal Corridor Association)
sites.address: I&M Canal Visitors’ Center, Gift Shop and Cafe: 754 First Street
sites.description: The Illinois and Michigan Canal, completed in 1848, extended 97 miles from Chicago to Peru-LaSalle. The Heritage Area united sixty communities in a network dedicated to preserving the memory of how important the canal was to the development of Illinois and the United States generally. Many of the member organizations have exhibits that document both the prehistory and history of this part of the Illinois Valley and neighboring regions affected by it.

sites.name: Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie
sites.address: Visitors’ Welcome Center: 30239 S. State Rte. 53
sites.hours: Trails: Daily 4AM-10PM; Welcome Center: Nov-Mar Mon-Fri 8AM-4:30PM; May-Oct Mon-Sat 8AM-4:30PM
sites.description: Visitors can learn about prairie ecology and early Native American inhabitants at the Welcome Center.

sites.name: Kankakee River State Park
sites.hours: Check website for current closure dates and hours
sites.description: The park includes several documented archaeological sites along the Kankakee River corridor.

sites.name: Kankakee County Historical Museum
sites.description: Permanent exhibits include American Indian artifacts related to cultural periods, with an extensive display of Potawatomi material from a nearby site.

sites.name: Camp Douglas
sites.address: South Martin Luther King Drive and E. 33rd St.
sites.description: Centered between 31st and 33rd Streets, north to south, and between Cottage Grove and King Drive, east to west, there is little evidence of Camp Douglas in the 2020s. However, during the Civil War it was the largest U.S. military facility in Illinois, serving variously as a training camp for Union soldiers, Confederate prisoner of war camp, and demobilization camp once fighting ended. Several archaeological projects confirmed the location and outlines of the camp.

sites.name: Stephen A. Douglas Tomb
sites.description: During his lifetime Senator Stephen A. Douglas was known as a fierce promoter of Illinois and Abraham Lincoln’s strongest rival. In recognition of his life of service he is buried in a mausoleum topped with a 46-foot-high column and tall statue of Senator Douglas.

sites.name: Oak Woods Cemetery
sites.description: The cemetery includes a mass grave of Confederate prisoners of war containing more than 4,000 burials.

sites.name: Sand Ridge Nature Center
sites.description: Interactive exhibits explain the dune-and-swale landscape and thousands of years of Native American history. Outdoor interpretive signs describe prehistoric settlement, transportation routes, and archaeological discoveries.
sites.notes: Includes interpretive signage such as the attached Thorn Creek Area panel.

sites.name: River Trail Nature Center
sites.description: Free exhibits include Native American artifacts. Nature trails interpret landscapes formed by the Des Plaines River.

sites.name: Dunn Museum
sites.description: Permanent exhibition 'The First People' presents 12,000 years of Native American history in Lake County through archaeology and continuing Indigenous traditions.

sites.name: Pokto Cinto (Serpent Twin)
sites.address: W Irving Park Rd, east of Des Plaines River Rd
sites.hours: Open when the park is open
sites.description: Earthwork effigy mound forming part of the 4000N interpretive trail celebrating Native American heritage, archaeology, and environmental stewardship.

sites.name: Oak Forest Heritage Preserve
sites.address: 159th St east of S Cicero Ave
sites.description: Interpretive trail describing archaeological investigations of a Native American village and the historic Cook County Poor Farm cemetery.

sites.name: Norwood Park Historical Society
sites.description: Museum exhibit 'Can You Dig It' displays artifacts excavated from the Noble-Seymour-Crippen House grounds, illustrating local historical archaeology.

sites.name: The Grove (Kennicott Grove)
sites.description: Nature preserve with interpretive trails describing Native American occupation of the area and archaeological discoveries through educational signage.
sites.notes: Recommended by Sara as an addition to Places of the Past.
